newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Teljoy shares jump on return to profit.
newsitem.headline: Teljoy shares jump on return to profit.

text.p: Teljoy shares leapt in early trade on Monday on the back of a surprisely strong turnaround in its year results back into profit, dealers said.
"It is on the back of the turnaround. All divisions are posting profits, even the smaller divisions," one dealer said.

The shares jumped 5.88 percent, or 25 cents, to 450 cents in thin volume before settling at 15 cents higher at 425 cents. It was the fourth most actively traded share on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and dealers saw volumes improving during the day.
Teljoy's pre-exceptional items earnings per share rose to 9.5 cents for the year ended March 31 from a 58.7 cents loss in the previous year.
Dealers said the the share price could rise further from these levels.
"The turnaround has not been priced into the market. Their results surprised the market," a dealer said.

Teljoy's chief executive Johann Pieterse said in a statement accompanying the results that both cellular phone and television divisions were expected to trade profitably and the group earnings before exceptional items would increase "substantially" in the new financial year.

"The health of the group has improved dramatically but it is too early to claim victory," he said, attributing the turnaround to "good basic housekeeping -- improving systems and administration, getting on top of the fraud problem, reducing bad debts and 'churn'".
